category_title: Quiet fourth-grade student with learning disabilities who prefers working alone and struggles with task initiation
minimal_context: Tyrone is sitting in the general classroom working on revising his draft to add creativity and interesting language.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Tyrone, it is time to revise your draft. Please add some creativity, interesting language, and feeling to your writing.

STUDENT: (Sits quietly without being able to start writing. He looks around, finding it difficult to concentrate in the noisy atmosphere of the classroom.)

TUTOR: What do you think you should write? Just put some of your ideas down on the paper.

STUDENT: (He has trouble generating and articulating ideas. He slowly writes on his paper: "I would read a book . play vido games with my brother .")

TUTOR: Okay, keep trying. Write some more to make it a cohesive story.

STUDENT: (He struggles with language fluency and gives up writing easily, just listing more disconnected events without clear focus: "I would play football with my friends . Then I will watch a movie with my mom and brother .")

options.A: Invite a professional writer to offer strategies for finding meaningful topics, demonstrate how to share a story, and host a public reading.
options.B: Provide individualized feedback and include comments on the student's draft to guide their revisions during the writing block.
options.C: Provide noncontingent attention to the student throughout the writing block and ignore the problem behaviors that function to gain attention.
options.D: Encourage "tootling" (reporting prosocial behavior) by providing a collective class reward when they reach a target number of "tootles" during the writing block.
